subject.title: Feature: Webchat / Control UI inline button support (buttons parameter, callback RPC, capabilities config)

question: Should WebChat inline interactions use shared presentation typed actions with a new authenticated `chat.callback` RPC, and should WebChat regain a capability/config key or rely on authenticated UI behavior without config?
rationale: The first implementation defines a public Gateway interaction contract, callback security semantics, and a possible replacement for a retired WebChat config surface, which automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Presentation plus authenticated RPC
options.body: Use shared presentation typed actions, add a scoped authenticated `chat.callback` RPC, avoid webhook routing in v1, and explicitly decide whether capability config exists.

options.title: Split protocol first
options.body: Approve the schema/RPC/auth contract first and leave Control UI rendering and click handling for a follow-up implementation issue.

options.title: Defer interactive WebChat
options.body: Keep WebChat text-only for now and route broader reactions/feedback work through the larger WebUI interaction tracker.

recommendation.title: Presentation plus authenticated RPC
recommendation.body: Use shared presentation typed actions, add a scoped authenticated `chat.callback` RPC, avoid webhook routing in v1, and explicitly decide whether capability config exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining blocker is product/API/security direction, and prior issue discussion routes that decision to steipete more strongly than current-line blame does.
